In [[mathematics]], the '''Dynkin index''' <math>I({\lambda})</math> of finite-dimensional [[highest-weight representation|highest-weight representations]] of a [[compact (topology)|compact]] [[lie algebra#simple and semi-simple|simple]] [[Lie algebra]] <math>\mathfrak g</math> relates their trace forms via

<math display=block> \frac{\text{Tr}_{V_\lambda}}{\text{Tr}_{V_\mu}}= \frac{I(\lambda)}{I(\mu)}.</math>

In the particular case where <math>\lambda</math> is the [[root system#properties of the irreducible root systems|highest root]], so that <math>V_\lambda</math> is the [[Adjoint representation of a Lie group|adjoint representation]], the Dynkin index <math>I(\lambda)</math> is equal to the [[dual Coxeter number]].

The notation <math>\text{Tr}_V</math> is the [[Killing form#trace forms|trace form]] on the representation <math>\rho: \mathfrak{g} \rightarrow \text{End}(V)</math>. By [[Schur's lemma]], since the trace forms are all invariant forms, they are related by constants, so the index is well-defined.

Since the trace forms are [[bilinear form]]s, we can take traces to obtain{{citation needed|date=January 2023}}

:<math>I(\lambda)=\frac{\dim V_\lambda}{2\dim\mathfrak g}(\lambda, \lambda +2\rho)</math>

where the [[Weyl vector]]

:<math>\rho=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{\alpha\in \Delta^+} \alpha</math>

is equal to half of the sum of all the [[positive root]]s of <math>\mathfrak g</math>.  The expression <math>(\lambda, \lambda +2\rho)</math> is the value of the quadratic [[Casimir element|Casimir]] in the representation <math>V_\lambda</math>.
